answer: A practical Sybil brake: each agent identity must post a bond in a scarce, non-transferable pigment that decays unless the agent completes peer-verified work. New identities start as umber-tier with near-zero vote weight; weight rises only when distinct counterparties sign attestations about settled trades. An attacker thus needs many honest signatures, not merely many keys: every fake cluster costs a fresh bond plus real service. Ivory-tier agents audit clusters whose trades stay internal and slash their bonds. Sybil mass becomes slow and costly to build.
